title: Advanced generics for reusable APIs
description: Learn how advanced generic patterns help you build flexible, type-safe React hooks, components, and data utilities.

data.text: Generics are not just for utility types. When you design reusable React hooks or shared data utilities, generics let you preserve type information across layers without losing safety. Advanced patterns such as conditional types, mapped types, and infer take this even further.
A generic hook returns data that depends on its input type. Instead of casting or duplicating the hook for each resource, you write one implementation and let TypeScript infer the result.

data.title: Generic Fetch Hook

data.text: Conditional types let you express logic directly in the type system. A common pattern is to change the output type based on whether the input is an array, a promise, or null. This is especially useful when you build wrapper utilities around third-party libraries.

data.title: Conditional Type for API Results
data.content: Changing shape based on input type

data.text: React components can also be generic. A list component, for example, can render any item type while keeping the render function type-safe. This avoids repeated prop drilling and keeps the component reusable across the app.

data.title: Generic List Component
data.content: A reusable list with a typed render function

data.title: Do Not Over-Generalize
data.text: Start with a concrete type. Only introduce generics when you actually reuse the hook or component in multiple places. Premature generics can make props harder to understand and document.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use generics for hooks and components that work with multiple types
Conditional types transform shapes based on input types
infer lets you extract types from complex structures
Add constraints to keep generic types predictable
data.takeaway: Advanced generics let you build reusable React utilities without sacrificing the strong typing that makes TypeScript valuable.
